text:
zara: FYI finance flagged an unexplained bump in unit cost for model-sku-12 after yesterday's routing rule change. can we triage?
kevin: saw the alert, roughly +14% cost/invocation for <64 token calls between 03:00-04:00 UTC.
lia: can you paste the econ query you used?
kevin: pasted below:

```
SELECT routing_policy, SUM(tokens) tokens, SUM(cost) cost, COUNT(*) calls
FROM econ_events
WHERE sku='sku-12' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-22T03:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-22T04:00:00Z'
GROUP BY routing_policy;
```

oscar: heatmap shows eu-central nodes had lower kv-hit during that hour. might be node-level imbalance.
metrics-bot: metric alert: sku-12 cache-affinity dropped 25% at 2026-03-22T03:12Z.
zara: did the routing rule cause fallbacks to a regional pool with cold caches?
lia: yes, rule v3 increases fallback aggressiveness when soft-quota hit. any quota events around that time?
kevin: quota logs show soft-throttles on tenant T-21 at 03:10 which would trigger fallback.
oscar: mitigation options: (1) rollback fallback aggressiveness, (2) prewarm fallback pool, (3) add a console diff view to compare policy A/B.
zara: for short term, can we run a quick canary to pin old rule and measure 30m?
metrics-bot: canary control created: routing-policy pinned to v2 for sku-12 on 10% of traffic. collecting 30m snapshots.
lia: long-term: add routing_policy_id to derived econ table and add per-node kv heatmap to cost dashboard. also surface sample rates.
kevin: agree. I'll open a ticket for backfill and a small RFC for console diff UX.
oscar: adding alert: if cache-affinity drop >15% AND cost/invocation increases >10% post-rollout, auto-pause fallback ramps.
zara: thanks all — will loop in finance after the canary finishes. closing thread for now.
